entities.summary: Arthur Lewis Watkins Sifton was a Canadian lawyer, judge and politician who served as the second premier of Alberta from 1910 until 1917. He became a minister in the federal cabinet of Canada thereafter. Born in Canada West, he grew up there and in Winnipeg, where he became a lawyer. He subsequently practised law with his brother Clifford Sifton in Brandon, where he was also active in municipal politics. He moved west to Prince Albert in 1885 and to Calgary in 1889. There, he was elected to the 4th and 5th North-West Legislative Assemblies; he served as a minister in the government of premier Frederick Haultain.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Arthur Sifton's tenure as premier of Alberta from 1910 to 1917 had significant regional impact, shaping provincial politics and governance. His subsequent role in the federal cabinet of Canada further solidified his influence on Canadian politics.
